column1: # ---- the cannon builtin's low half was unreachable in every capture ----

column6: REAL, and the report named only HALF of it. Setting 249 (varbit 14176, the threshold) was never written by any cannon drive and its default is 0, which `threshold > 0` refuses -- but writing it alone changes NOTHING, measured: with 14176=12 in force and reading back 12, the chat band is pixel-identical to the shipped capture, because the drive's only ammunition movement was loc op 3 taking 15 to 0 in ONE tick and `ammo == 0` returns before the low test is reached. The low edge needs the fire clock, and the fire clock needs a target the fixture tile has none of. New `cannonlow-*` rows add `::spawn goblin 5` (five guaranteed firing ticks, so 15 -> 12 on the third whatever the damage rolls) and drop the loc op; all four toplevels now photograph `Your cannon is running low on cannonballs: 12 left.` The `cannon-*` rows keep the empty edge and now carry the threshold too, which turns the ABSENCE of a low line there into the `ammo == 0` precedence rule instead of a vacuous silence

REAL. `sim_varbit:` and `sim_oploc:` were TORIRS_LOG, and OPT=1 compiles -DNDEBUG which compiles TORIRS_LOG away -- every capture in this directory is OPT=1, so the only receipt two drive levers have was absent from every log while `sim_cmd:` beside them printed. `strings` on the pre-fix torirs_gate finds neither string; on this one it finds both. That is why CANNON-01 had to be read off the jobs file rather than the log, and the reads-back field is what separates `the profile declares no such varbit` from `the value is too wide for its bits`
